dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the bargaining brief and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The union-floor hot desks review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I drafted a wage proposal in the union conference room after reviewing the bargaining history alone.
What made the proposal usable?
I could hold the trade-offs in view through the final paragraph.
Someone new shadowed me in the Tuesday mediation this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the union conference room into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
During last year's grievance preparation, I tried to write the bargaining brief at a hot desk while stewards kept asking for updates.
What happened to the brief?
I contradicted the seniority concession and had to rebuild the argument that night.
I answer routine contract-status messages from the union floor without difficulty.
So the floor is not always a problem?
No, it works for messages that do not require a negotiating position.
I archived last cycle's notes on the union-floor hot desks and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The union conference room is occupied all Tuesday, while mediation starts at 15:00.
Do you have another quiet room?
Not in the building before the session.
A vendor call about the bargaining brief ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the Tuesday mediation checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the union conference room.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the union-floor hot desks records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
During a contract-renewal week, I drafted at the union-floor desk between steward questions and reversed two linked wage positions in the same brief.
How did you discover it?
The lead negotiator spotted the conflict just before the meeting.
I sketched next week's plan for the union conference room before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the bargaining brief updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The mediation chair has asked for the final brief by 13:30 so both sides can read it before the 15:00 session.
Can the drafting be repaired later?
No, the review window closes before mediation begins.
I compared two options for the union-floor hot desks tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the Tuesday mediation handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Why should I decline the union-floor hot desk on Tuesday when the bargaining brief must be ready for mediation?
